author: Giovanni Battista Astria
text: The fire that burns within my heart does not permit me, as a son to so loving a father, to withhold the good desires that burn continually within my breast.

author: Lelio Antoglietta
text: Know, Your Paternity, that for no short time the talent of the Second Vocation has burned within my breast, which God has given to me, most unworthy of such a talent.

author: Ignazio Balami
text: I hope to make myself holy by this road.

author: Pietro Comentali
text: I wrote of a desire which the Lord had given me to spend even my life in the help of souls in the Indies.

author: Pietro Comentali
text: Would that I could send you the heart within this letter, that it might show you in person how great the desire is.

author: Diego Camassa
text: Receive, Your Paternity, this son of yours, unworthy though he be, at your feet, whence he will not depart until he has finished the cause of God.

author: Pietro Comentali
text: Yet Your Paternity could send me as a penance for my sins, which will be the greatest contentment I can ever desire or have in this life.

author: Pietro Comentali
text: For the rest, ure et seca — burn and cut. For I neither wish nor desire any other consolation in this life.

author: Antonio Rondonio
text: I humbly beseech you to grant me the permission to go thither, though unworthy. Nor refuse, for God has shown to me in prayer that in those parts I must die a martyr.

author: Diego Camassa
text: I burn, my Father, I burn, and I write it with tears in my eyes. Behold my heart in the hands and at the feet of Your Paternity, with all indifference.

author: Diego Camassa
text: I feel, Father, the blaze grown each day ever greater in my heart, and it inflames me to this noble conquest. Let me follow my Captain to the Indies, for it is time.

author: Diego Camassa
text: I do not seek it for myself, but for Jesus Christ crucified and for the Holy Church of God.

author: Diego Camassa
text: I put myself in the hands and at the feet of Your Paternity, with total indifference in all that you shall dispose of me.

author: Diego Camassa
text: I present to you that most precious blood of Christ crucified; the salvation of infinite souls; and of my own soul. I shall be an apostle, for so God wills.

author: Diego Camassa
text: This alone makes me, instead of sighing continually, remain secure and cheerful; and I console myself that we are not the masters of God's glory.

author: Francesco Barletta
text: May our Lord give to Your Paternity the completion and the crown of your holy labors.

author: Marco Stella
text: What shall I say of the ardent longing to shed my blood for Him who first shed it for me in love on a hard Cross? What of the zeal for so many souls that are lost, which break and melt my heart?

author: Marco Stella
text: O my sweetest Father, I feel an interior voice telling me that now is the time. O happy my soul, if I shall have it, on such an occasion, for love of the blessed Jesus, to lose — or rather, to gain.

author: Marco Stella
text: For love of the Lord, remember this unworthy slave of the Holy Society, and admit me to the number of those chosen for this Holy Mission. O my Father, with how many tears do I write this!

author: Marco Stella
text: When I was still a child, in the darkness of Egypt, the Lord communicated this desire to me; indeed this was the sole motive for which I entered the Most Holy Society.

author: Daniello Bartoli
text: This desire has remained ever most lively in my heart, and has grown since I entered this holy order, twelve years now.

author: Francesco Giuseppe Bressani
text: There is not yet extinguished amid the ice of my so many failings that little warmth with which the Lord kindled my heart when He gave me the holy desire of the Indies.

author: Leonardo Cinami
text: What use is it to spur us on, if then You would put the bridle on us just as we are about to run?

author: Domenico Arganantio
text: Oh, how my heart has been inflamed with living flames of desire to suffer for the love of my crucified Lord!

author: Giacomo Antonio Basile
text: Behold me, Father, ready for all things.

author: Domenico Arcolino
text: I would have wished to show it by imprinting on this sheet characters formed of my own blood, had Obedience not forbidden it.

author: Luigi Spinelli
text: O how I speak from the heart, Our Father! O that I were in Rome, that I might show you how I burn with desire, and what courage the Lord gives me to go and suffer and labor for His holy name!

author: Luigi Spinelli
text: Believe me, Your Paternity, that I burn and am consumed with desire, and every moment seems to me a thousand years.

author: Luigi Spinelli
text: My crucified Christ, grant that soon, soon, soon, through Your infinite mercy, I may be consoled.

author: Luigi Spinelli
text: Our Father, I can say nothing else in this letter but that I am dying of desire, and I sigh the whole day long. O God, when shall I be consoled!

author: Luigi Spinelli
text: Shall distance deny me what the goodness of the Lord and the charity of Your Paternity promise me? God forbid.

author: Giacomo Lazari
text: I have placed myself in the hands of holy obedience. This I ask, this I seek, and either I shall obtain it or die of pure desire.

author: Leonardo Cinami
text: May Our Lord grant Your Paternity long life for His glory, and to me only as much as will let me reach the Indies and shed my blood for the faith.

author: Leonardo Cinami
text: I close with Your Paternity, but my tears do not end, which I cast continuously at the feet of the crucifix for this which I call beatitude in this life.

author: Sebastiano Berni
text: What costs Your Paternity so little may buy me Paradise.

author: Sebastiano Berni
text: Pater mi, ecce ego, mitte me — Father, here I am, send me.

author: Sebastiano Berni
text: When I heard the news of the martyrs, oh, how I longed not only to go but to have gone long ago!

author: Sebastiano Berni
text: Kneeling I beg you that, if so you judge for the greater glory of God, you leave me not behind.
